teaching_gems.gem: Rewrite Newtonian gravity in the index language of relativity (a tidal tensor acting on a separation, vacuum law as zero trace) before touching curvature.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Learners meet the structure of the answer in a theory they already trust, so the relativistic equation looks like an upgrade rather than an arbitrary new law.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Equation morph: the Newtonian deviation equation smoothly transforms symbol by symbol into (10.23), with each replacement (dot to D/Dtau, Hessian to Riemann contraction) highlighted and explained on hover.

teaching_gems.gem: Redo the familiar lift experiments with two balls instead of one.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A single extra ball turns a picture about the equivalence principle into a picture about what equivalence cannot remove, motivating curvature without any mathematics.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Lift lab with four cases and a precision slider; learner predicts, then observes, which cases show drift.

teaching_gems.gem: Guess the field equation from the analogy, then strengthen the guess by requiring it for every possible observer direction.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Shows how a physically motivated scalar condition becomes a tensor equation, a reusable move in theory-building.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Light-cone widget: learner rotates a timelike vector V inside the cone while a symmetric 2x2 or 4x4 matrix is adjusted; a readout of V.R.V turns green only when it vanishes for all V, which happens only for the zero matrix.

teaching_gems.gem: Mixed partials commute, therefore the tangent and separation vectors commute, therefore relative acceleration is given by the curvature commutator.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A short chain from a fact every calculus student knows to the geometric heart of the derivation.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Flow-box closure demo: step along V then xi and back; the quadrilateral closes on a coordinate grid, then parallel transport around it reveals curvature.

teaching_gems.gem: Check that g_00 is not a coordinate artefact by applying a slow-motion-compatible infinitesimal coordinate change.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Teaches the habit of asking which quantities are physical before matching to observation, a precursor to gauge thinking in linearized gravity.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Gauge playground: sliders for the components of X^a(x); a table of h_ab updates live, with h_00 staying fixed at first order when the slow-motion constraint is on and changing when it is switched off.

teaching_gems.gem: A freely falling observer's lab is an orthonormal tetrad whose spatial axes are gyroscopes.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Gives an operational meaning to frame components and explains why tides appear as R^i_0j0.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Animated capsule orbiting a planet with three gyroscope arrows and a cloud of test particles; frame-component readouts of the separation compared with the tidal matrix.

teaching_gems.gem: Summarize a long derivation as a numbered chain of principles and ask the learner to label each link.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Converts a sequence of calculations into a memorable argument structure and exposes which assumptions are physical and which mathematical.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Drag-and-drop map: six steps as cards and principles (equivalence, geodesic postulate, covariance, correspondence, tidal variation, contraction) as labels to attach; feedback explains mismatches.

teaching_gems.gem: Pick the geometric side of the sourced equations by matching the divergence-free property of energy-momentum.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Shows why the Einstein tensor, not the Ricci tensor, sits on the left once matter is present, using an identity the learner has already proved.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Side-by-side 'conservation check': for a sample metric the app computes nabla_b R^ab and nabla_b G^ab numerically, showing only the latter vanishes identically.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Printed p.183 quotes Poisson's equation with 8 pi G rho, whereas the book's own (4.5) has 4 pi G rho.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Confuses the origin of the 8 pi in kappa and may lead to wrong Newtonian-limit checks.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: State Poisson as nabla^2 phi = 4 pi G rho and show that the 8 pi in kappa arises because R_00 = kappa(T_00 - (1/2) T g_00) = (1/2) kappa rho c^2 must equal nabla^2 phi/c^2.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: §10.4 says the Newtonian K is defined by (10.11); the definition is (10.9).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: A reader following the reference finds the trace condition instead of the definition.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Cite (10.9) for the definition and (10.11) for the trace condition.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Equation (10.38) is printed with D^2 in the denominator without tau.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Minor, but the typesetting makes the absolute derivative unclear.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The reduced Newtonian-limit deviation equation on printed p.182 omits the factor eta^beta in the Hessian term.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Restore eta^beta: d^2 eta^alpha/dt^2 + delta^{alpha gamma} d_gamma d_beta phi eta^beta = 0.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: In the computation of R^alpha_0gamma0 the text writes (1/2) epsilon times second derivatives of g_00; the epsilon belongs with h_00.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Readers doing order counting may think an extra factor of epsilon is present.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Write (1/2) epsilon d_gamma d_alpha h_00 = (1/2) d_gamma d_alpha g_00.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Equation (10.16) prints xi^alpha where xi^a is meant, and the step replacing partial by covariant derivatives silently requires a symmetric (torsion-free) connection.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Index-type confusion (Greek means spatial in this chapter) and a hidden assumption.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Correct the index and state explicitly that the Christoffel terms cancel because Gamma^a_bc = Gamma^a_cb.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The claim that the Ricci tensor is the only meaningful contraction of Riemann is left as '(why?)', and the proportionality G^ab = kappa T^ab is only suggested, not derived; the possibility of a cosmological term is not mentioned until Chapter 13.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may believe the field equations are logically forced by conservation alone.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show the contraction argument using Riemann symmetries, and note that Lambda g^ab is also divergence-free; mention Lovelock's theorem as the rigorous uniqueness statement in four dimensions.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The tidal picture in Figs. 10.3-10.4 shows only sideways convergence; stretching along the direction of fall is never mentioned.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may think tides only squeeze, and miss that a trace-free tidal tensor must stretch in some direction to compensate.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show a ring or sphere of particles deforming into an ellipsoid with eigenvalues (+1, +1, -2) GM/r^3 and link the zero sum to Laplace's equation.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Bold frame indices versus roman coordinate indices carry the whole meaning of §10.5, but the typographic distinction is subtle and disappears in handwriting, plain text and OCR (the reading copy garbles (10.29) and (10.36)).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Frequent misreading of e_i^a versus e^i_a and of which index is summed.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: In the app use hats or parentheses for frame indices (e.g. e_(i)^a) and colour-code frame versus coordinate indices.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Geodesic deviation is easy to get with the wrong sign when mixing sources. The book's form D^2 xi^a/Dtau^2 - R^a_bcd V^b V^c xi^d = 0 is the same equation as the MTW-style D^2 xi^a/Dtau^2 + R^a_bcd V^b xi^c V^d = 0 (swap the last two Riemann indices, which flips the sign); both use R^a_bcd = d_c Gamma^a_bd - ... . Real sign differences appear only for books with other Riemann or Ricci conventions (e.g. Weinberg).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners who compare only the visible sign, not the index order, may think the books disagree, or may combine a different Riemann convention with this equation and get convergence and divergence reversed.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Compare index order and the Riemann definition before comparing signs, and sanity-check with the Newtonian limit: for a point mass K = Hessian of phi has eigenvalue -2GM/r^3 radially (stretching) and +GM/r^3 transversely (squeezing).

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The step from 'R_ab V^a V^b = 0 along geodesics' to 'for every timelike vector at every point' relies on existence of a geodesic through any point with any timelike tangent, stated briefly; the polarization proof itself is left to Exercise 10.6.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: The logical strength of the argument is easy to miss.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Spell out the polarization identity: for symmetric S, S(u,w) = [S(u+w,u+w) - S(u-w,u-w)]/4, and note that timelike vectors span the space.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Parallel transport of gyroscope spin is asserted with citations rather than shown, and the book's further reading cites Hartle with two different dates. The result is now experimentally confirmed by Gravity Probe B, which the text does not mention.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Physical motivation for the non-rotating frame feels like an authority argument.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Add a short explanation (spin 4-vector orthogonal to u, no torque, hence Fermi-Walker transport, which reduces to parallel transport on geodesics) and cite Gravity Probe B.

tutor_notes: Open with: 'If you were sealed in a falling lift, could you ever tell that a planet is nearby?' Let the learner discover that two balls, not one, are needed.
Before any tensors, have the learner derive the Newtonian tidal equation by subtracting two copies of F = ma; check they see that only second derivatives of phi appear.
Ask the learner to compute the tidal matrix for a point mass on the z-axis and verify its trace is zero; connect the negative eigenvalue to stretching along the radial line.
When deriving geodesic deviation, keep a checklist of why each term vanishes (geodesic condition, zero bracket); learners often lose track of which assumption kills which term.
Check understanding of the analogy with a matching exercise: dots to D/Dtau, eta to xi, Hessian of phi to R^a_cbd V^c V^d, zero trace to R_ab V^a V^b = 0.
Probe the promotion step: 'Why is R_ab V^a V^b = 0 for one observer not enough?' Expect an answer involving arbitrary timelike directions and symmetry.
Pre-empt the 'Ricci-flat means flat' error by asking whether there are tides above the Earth where nabla^2 phi = 0.
For §10.6, have the learner fill a table of terms in the geodesic equation with their order in epsilon before looking at the book's conclusion.
Emphasize that g_00 = 1 + 2 phi/c^2 came from motion, not field equations; then ask what additional input is needed to relate phi to mass density (answer: the field equations with source).
Warn about the misprinted 8 pi G rho on printed p.183 and about sign conventions when the learner consults other textbooks.

Common learner questions: Why the Einstein tensor rather than Ricci on the left with matter? Why is there a factor 8 pi? What is a tetrad physically? Why are bold and plain indices different? Have short answers ready tied to the chapter's equations.
End-of-unit check: ask the learner to narrate Einstein's six-step route and name the principle behind each step (Exercise 10.11).
